chunks: My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mu'adhdhi from 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub from 'Amr ibn Thabit from 'Amr ibn 'Ikrimah who said:

We spent the night when Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed in Medina, and behold, a freedman of ours was saying: We heard yesterday a caller calling out and saying: O the killers, in ignorance, of Husayn! Glad tidings of punishment and scourging! All the people of the sky are invoking curse upon you, from every prophet and messenger and tribe. You have been cursed on the tongue of the son of David and the Spirit, bearer of the Gospel.

key_terms.لَيْلَةَ قُتِلَ الْحُسَيْنُ: The night when Husayn was killed

ai.seo_question: What did the caller announce regarding the curse on the killers of Imam Husayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic dimension of the Karbala tragedy, where the jinn publicly announce the curse upon Husayn's killers, linking their fate to the prophetic tradition. It specifically invokes the curse of Jesus (Isa), the son of David, and Gabriel (Dh al-Ruh), emphasizing the continuity of divine retribution across different eras of revelation. This underscores the Shia belief that the martyrdom of the Ahl al-Bayt resonates throughout the heavens and earth, involving both human and jinn witnesses.
